summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with HCV cirrhosis, was admitted for increasing abdominal distension and hematuria. Imaging confirmed large ascites and cholelithiasis without cholecystitis. A paracentesis removed 2.5 liters of fluid, which showed no signs of infection, ruling out spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. His hematuria resolved during admission and was attributed to low platelets from cirrhosis and HCV therapy. Due to persistent thrombocytopenia, his ribavirin, interferon, and filgrastim were discontinued. Diuretic therapy was intensified with furosemide and spironolactone, and he was advised on a strict low-salt diet. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans to follow up with hepatology and urology.
